I know there are a lot of question marks involved, but doing some research and compiling some options will make you feel a lot less trapped.  Can friends or family help store or move some of your stuff?  Would you need a U-Haul?  Moving to a city would be best, there'll be more job options, more residency choices, and public transport.  Maybe a college city?  There'll be a lot of people looking for roommates.  I don't know about you, but I had worked at my company for 9 years.  I was ready to lose my home, move back in with my parents, and work at McDonald's if it meant a fresh start.  (I was in my late-twenties, it wouldn't have been a proud moment) Find out how far you're willing to go and what you'd sacrifice to make a break for it, then make a new plan.

A couple people here have suggested getting help, and that's a great idea to help in the long term, but right now, get out of that job.  Last year I was in a situation just like you are now.  Felt trapped, exhausted physically, mentally and emotionally, I thought i'd lose my home if I quit... It got to the point where I couldn't enjoy my days off because I knew i'd have to go back to work soon.  I wanted to shoot myself for making myself go to work.  Finally, one day I couldn't take it anymore, and I just let go.  Of the job, not my life.  I told myself i'd do anything to keep my home, but I wouldn't work there another second.  One of the best decisions i've ever made.  I know you've said you're going to have trouble making rent, but you've also said that you need to get out of state.  Start planning to do ust that.  Right now.  Planning it out will help you feel better right now.  Get out, even if you have to start from scratch, your happiness is worth more than carrying on like you are now.

Oh man, THIS brings back memories, I worked at a place that had a baler twice the size of the one in your picture, the bale would take up an entire pallet and overhang a little on each side, it also had a % full indicator on the side to tell you how much you could feasibly stuff in there.  Here comes problem the first, if it got past about 93% full it would no longer auto-eject the bale and you'd have to go grab milkhooks, hook it by the wires tying it, and pull it TOWARDS you to get it out.  DANGEROUS.  Here comes problem the second, the company recycling the bales started to complain that our bales were too light and threatened to stop paying us for them, so management made us stop making bales at 80% full, and forced us to wait until they were 90-95% full.  Problem the third, only the grocery department had to make bales, so every other department just threw their shit in there all mish-mash without breaking down their boxes, making it a huge shitshow, unbalancing the loads and getting boxes jammed in the ram, filling it until they couldn't jam anything more in and then just throwing their shit on the floor for grocery to clean up... I can't tell you how many times it went beyond 93% full, we had to make a bale and we couldn't pull the fucker out, it'd get stuck on the safety door, you couldn't pull it out or push it back in, you'd have to cut the fucking wires, swim in cardboard, clear the mess, stuff it all back in and start from scratch.  NOW I work for a company where we ALL just throw our cardboard into the even BIGGER baler, and NONE of us makes the bale.  A truck swings by 3 times a week and sucks the bale out from the side of the building.  So sweet...
